claims.statement: A 2024 Canadian border-agency audit found two duplicate pairs among ten sampled potential pairs even though the accounting system had built-in controls for matching vendor, invoice number and amount.

A UK public-sector case processed 645,000 historical transactions, used a senior recovery auditor to verify and recover 82 exceptions, and recovered a six-figure sum, showing buyer demand and material human work but not a Polish SME base rate.
A published UK duplicate-payment recovery price lists a 25% standard fee and 12.5% minimum fee on recoveries, supporting contingent pricing but not the proposed Polish monitoring price.
SAP documents a similarity-based duplicate control and Dynamics documents configurable invoice matching; fuzzy detection and exception workflows are incumbent features, not scarce technology.

A 2025 UK award for duplicate-payment software serving about 250,000 invoices annually across four partners and two council-owned customers was worth GBP 141,600 over four years; it evidences a high-volume software budget but not a Polish SME price.

Recovery consultants act on behalf of the buyer, and official guidance calls for robust scrutiny, written agreement and fair handling of counterclaims; an anomaly vendor does not itself hold recovery authority.

Statistics Poland counted 17,601 active enterprises with 50-249 employees in Q4 2024, but this broad denominator does not reveal invoice volumes, ERP fragmentation, recovery propensity or willingness to buy.

Where invoice exports contain personal data, GDPR Article 28 requires a processor contract and safeguards; Polish unjust-enrichment law provides a recovery basis but also enumerates cases where repayment cannot be demanded.

contrary_evidence: SAP already markets similarity-based duplicate controls, so entity resolution alone is reproducible and bundleable.
The strongest recovery case involved 645,000 transactions and a senior auditor; it does not demonstrate economical recovery for a firm with only several thousand invoices.
Contingency compensation can encourage invalid or overaggressive claims, requiring buyer oversight and written supplier agreement.
The public software award is for a shared high-volume council setting and cannot validate per-SME pricing.

economics.acquisition_route: Begin with five no-upfront-fee closed-period audits through warm construction and field-service contacts, then test accountants, fractional CFOs and ERP implementers with a written referral offer. No partner commitment, conversion rate or channel CAC is evidenced.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A requirement, not a forecast: 150 customers at 36,000 PLN recurring annual revenue produce 5.4m PLN ARR. At a 30% normalized owner-earnings margin, 80% founder ownership and a 3x earnings value, founder equity is about 3.89m PLN, still below 5m before liabilities; more than 1.11m PLN of non-double-counted after-tax distributions or stronger economics would be needed. Reaching 150 customers equals about 0.85% of Poland's 17,601 medium active enterprises before invoice-volume and sector filters, so a 7-9 year path depends on unproven channel access, retention and margins.
economics.founder_time: Limit the initial service to two concurrent clients and at most 4 hours per day, automate ingestion and evidence assembly, and require customer finance staff to approve and pursue every claim. Contract data-security and legal review; do not promise urgent or unbounded recovery support.
economics.gross_margin_basis: The service is not software-only: an official case used a senior recovery auditor plus statement review, verification and recovery work. Model 45-60% gross margin for early audits and 70-80% only for mature monitoring after confirmation workflows are delegated; both require measurement.
economics.payback: Customer payback is aligned when fees are payable only from recovered cash. Founder CAC payback is unknown; require each channel cohort to recover sales and onboarding cost within six months before scaling.
economics.pricing: Evidence supports a fee tied to actual recoveries: a published UK price lists a 25% standard and 12.5% minimum recovery fee. Test 20-25% in Poland and charge nothing on unconfirmed flags. The proposed 1,500-4,000 PLN monthly monitoring fee remains an assumption and should follow a paid audit.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Historical recovery is one-off and repeat audits should yield less after controls improve. Retention depends on proving that pre-payment monitoring prevents enough new loss to justify a fixed fee; no Polish retention evidence exists.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A permissioned, privacy-preserving library of adjudicated vendor aliases, invoice-number transformations, credit-note patterns and false-positive explanations could improve precision; client-specific data rights and incumbent fuzzy controls mean this compounds only if transferable features and measured lift survive privacy and contract restrictions.
fingerprint.customer: Polish firms with 50-500 employees, multiple entities or branches and at least several thousand supplier invoices per year, beginning with construction and field-service groups.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Accounting firms, ERP implementers and fractional CFOs are proposed resellers; construction and renewable-installation contacts provide an initial low-trust-distance test segment, but no channel commitment or CAC evidence exists.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Air-gapped or tightly isolated analysis of AP, payment, supplier-master and credit-note exports, with explainable candidate pairs, bank-change alerts and recovery evidence packets; a one-off contingent audit may convert to recurring pre-payment monitoring, while the customer retains supplier contact, settlement and payment authority.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The CFO pays a percentage of cash actually recovered after customer confirmation and, only after value is demonstrated, a fixed fee for an exception queue reviewed by the customer's finance team before payment release.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A year-end audit, ERP migration, supplier dispute or pre-payment run creates a need to identify duplicate or erroneous disbursements that configured ERP controls missed.

founder_fit: Entity resolution, fuzzy matching and anomaly ranking directly fit the founder's data-science background.
A read-only pilot can be built within available capital without taking custody of funds.
The founder can cap work at two concurrent audits and keep supplier communications with customer finance while employed.
The weak point is commercial and recovery operations: proposed accountant and ERP channels are uncommitted, and human validation must be productized or delegated.
risks: False or poorly documented claims can damage supplier relationships and create counterclaims.
Sensitive bank, supplier and invoice data create security, confidentiality and GDPR obligations.
Recovery can become a manual service business if statements, contracts and customer confirmation are not standardized.
Incumbent ERP and AP platforms can bundle similar detection and approval features.
The broad company-count denominator may conceal a much smaller viable segment.

structure.commercial_archetype: Contingency-fee recovery audit converting to financial-control SaaS
structure.control_point: The explainable exception queue reviewed before payment release and the evidence packet used by the customer's finance team to reclaim agreed past overpayments
structure.critical_dependency: Complete, joinable AP/payment/supplier exports, a controller-processor contract where personal data is present, and customer finance authority to validate, contact suppliers and recover agreed amounts

thesis: Run a privacy-conscious, read-only recovery audit for Polish mid-market firms that finds fuzzy duplicate invoices, unapplied credits, bank-detail anomalies and contract mismatches, then offers pre-payment monitoring. Official audits and procurements establish that leakage can survive internal controls and that buyers pay both contingent recovery fees and monitoring-software budgets, but the evidence does not establish a Polish mid-market recovery rate, channel CAC or subscription conversion. The paid event is confirmed cash recovery or a customer-approved pre-payment exception process, not anomaly flags.
title: Read-Only Accounts-Payable Recovery Audit for Mid-Market SMEs
uncertainties: The recoverable-error rate, recovery time and supplier cooperation rate in Polish 50-500 employee firms remain unknown.
The minimum annual invoice count and spend for contribution-positive human-reviewed audits remain unknown.
No accountant, ERP implementer or fractional-CFO channel has committed, so CAC, lead flow and revenue share are unknown.
Audit-to-monitoring conversion, monitoring price and retention are unknown.
Whether cross-client alias and adjudication features can be retained and transferred under customer contracts is unknown.
